plan.contextChunk: This figure traces the operation of merge sort on an eight-element array as a bottom-up lattice of gray boxes linked by thick gray arrows. The bottom rank, tagged "initial sequence", holds eight single-element squares reading 5, 2, 4, 7, 1, 3, 2, 6 from left to right. Pairs of arrows, each pair captioned "merge", lift adjacent squares into four two-element boxes reading 2 5, 4 7, 1 3, and 2 6. A second rank of merge arrows combines those into two four-element boxes, 2 4 5 7 and 1 2 3 6. A last pair of arrows, again captioned "merge", brings both into the wide box at the top, tagged "sorted sequence", which reads 1 2 2 3 4 5 6 7. Box width scales with the run it holds, so the doubling of sorted-run length shows up directly as the boxes widen from rank to rank while their count halves. Read upward, the drawing presents the algorithm as repeated merging of already-sorted runs.

interactionPlan.concept: Merge sort builds a sorted sequence by repeatedly merging adjacent already-sorted runs, doubling run length at each level, and the inner merge routine must compare the two fronts and take the smaller (using <= on ties) to stay correct and stable.
elements: bottom label 'initial sequence'
rank of eight single-element gray squares reading 5, 2, 4, 7, 1, 3, 2, 6 left to right
four two-element gray boxes reading 2 5, 4 7, 1 3, 2 6
two four-element gray boxes reading 2 4 5 7 and 1 2 3 6
top wide gray box reading 1 2 2 3 4 5 6 7 with label 'sorted sequence' above it
thick gray upward arrows linking each pair of child boxes to its parent merged box
the caption 'merge' beside each converging arrow pair (seven merge sites total)
box widths scaling with run length so runs visibly widen and halve in count per rank
highlight overlay marking the active child pair, their merge arrow, and the destination box during step-through
stability tags 2ᴸ (left-half origin) and 2ᴿ (right-half origin) on the two duplicate 2 values when the trace is on

interactions.label: Merge call
interactions.teaches: Stepping in post-order (all four singleton merges, then the two half merges, then the root merge) shows the recursion order: a parent run is only built once both child runs are already sorted, and run length doubles at every level

interactions.label: Implement merge(left, right)

api.does: true when left's front element <= right's front element (<= on ties is what keeps the merge stable)
append left's front element to the output run and advance left's front pointer — the only way to consume left
append right's front element to the output run and advance right's front pointer
true when left has no elements remaining
true when right has no elements remaining
append all remaining elements of the named side ('left' or 'right') to the output in order

interactions.frame: the two input runs drawn side by side with a front-pointer on each, plus the output run growing by exactly one element per recorded step, with the just-taken element and the comparison that chose it highlighted
interactions.success_check: the output run is nondecreasing AND, with the stability trace on, the left-origin 2 (2ᴸ) appears before the right-origin 2 (2ᴿ)
interactions.teaches: The merge inner loop is just 'compare the two fronts, emit the smaller, advance that side, then drain the survivor' — and using <= (not <) on the comparison is precisely what preserves the original order of equal keys

interactions.label: Stability trace
interactions.teaches: Tagging the two equal 2s by their half of origin makes stability observable during the run: a correct (<=) merge keeps 2ᴸ ahead of 2ᴿ in the final row, while a strict-< merge swaps them

demo_steps.title: The merge lattice
demo_steps.narration: Read bottom-up: eight singletons merge pairwise into sorted 2-runs, those into 4-runs, and finally into the one sorted 8-run. Each rank doubles the run length while halving the number of boxes.

demo_steps.title: Step the merge calls
demo_steps.narration: Advance the merge-call stepper in post-order. Watch the highlighted child pair, its 'merge' arrow, and the destination box: a parent run appears only after both children are already sorted.

demo_steps.title: Run the merge routine
demo_steps.narration: On the headline merge (2 4 5 7 | 1 2 3 6), step the code frame by frame: each step compares the two fronts and appends the smaller, then drains whichever side survives.

demo_steps.title: See stability
demo_steps.narration: Turn the stability trace on and rerun. The two equal 2s are tagged by origin; a <= comparison keeps 2ᴸ before 2ᴿ, while switching to the buggy strict-< version lets 2ᴿ jump ahead — stability lives entirely in that one comparison.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Merge sort's correctness comes from merging already-sorted runs, and its stability comes from a single detail in the inner loop: on a tie, take from the left run (use <=), which keeps equal keys in their original relative order.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the four-rank lattice of light-gray boxes with thin black borders; box width proportional to the number of elements so runs visibly widen upward while their count halves (8 → 4 → 2 → 1). Connect each parent to its two children with thick medium-gray upward arrows and place the italic caption 'merge' at each of the seven convergence points. Top box labeled 'sorted sequence' (1 2 2 3 4 5 6 7), bottom row labeled 'initial sequence' (5 2 4 7 1 3 2 6). For the step-through overlay, tint the active child pair, their arrow, and the destination box in a warm accent (e.g. amber) while dimming the rest. For the stability trace, render the two duplicate 2s with small superscript origin tags (2ᴸ in blue, 2ᴿ in orange) and carry those colors into the code-editor's output run so the order of the two 2s is legible frame by frame. Keep the code-editor panel docked beside the lattice, showing the two input runs with front pointers and the growing output row.

discrepancies: Every interactive control (demo-step ◀/▶ buttons, the 'Merge call' dropdown, the 'Stability trace' checkbox, the Sample/Buggy/Starter tabs, the Run button, and the playback controls) is wired with inline onclick/onchange handlers that resolve against the global scope, but all of those handler functions (prevStep, nextStep, update_mergeStep, toggle_stabilityTrace, switchTab, runCode, playFirst/Prev/Next/Toggle) are declared inside the wrapping IIFE and never assigned to window — so each click throws a ReferenceError and has no effect.

The merge lattice is compressed into roughly the left half of the viewport because the control panel occupies the right half, making the boxes and the italic 'merge' labels noticeably smaller than in the source's full-width composition.
The merge-trace overlay is drawn at y≈640 inside the same 800×750 viewbox, immediately below the 'initial sequence' caption (y≈608), so an active run crowds that bottom label.
evaluation.notes: The lattice itself is a faithful, numerically exact reproduction of the source (correct values at every rank, gray boxes/arrows, seven italic 'merge' labels, sorted/initial captions) and the planned interactions — post-order merge stepping, a stability trace on the duplicate 2s, and a worker-backed merge code editor with frame playback — are conceptually excellent; however, because none of the handler functions are exposed on window, every on-page control is dead at runtime, which is the figure's single most damaging flaw.
action_items: Expose all UI handlers on the global scope (e.g. window.prevStep=prevStep; window.nextStep=nextStep; window.update_mergeStep=update_mergeStep; window.toggle_stabilityTrace=toggle_stabilityTrace; window.switchTab=switchTab; window.runCode=runCode; window.playFirst=playFirst; window.playPrev=playPrev; window.playNext=playNext; window.playToggle=playToggle;) or move them outside the IIFE, so the inline onclick/onchange attributes actually fire.
Give the lattice more horizontal room (e.g. dock the control panel below or as an overlay, or widen the SVG container) so box and 'merge'-label sizes match the source's full-width layout.
Move the merge-trace band lower or reserve dedicated vertical space so it does not collide with the 'initial sequence' caption when a run is active.

feedback.rationale: The concept and plan are excellent (concept_accuracy 5, no plan action items), but all interactivity is broken due to a single implementation bug — handler functions trapped inside an IIFE are unreachable by inline onclick attributes — plus minor layout spacing issues, all fixable by the generator without changing the plan.

discrepancies: The merge-sort tree is rendered noticeably narrower and taller than the source's wide landscape layout (rows compressed horizontally into a ~square aspect inside the 600x740 viewbox), so the overall proportions differ from the original
The italic 'merge' labels are smaller and sit closer to the arrow shafts than in the source, where they are larger and clearly centered in the gap between each arrow pair

The default (step 1) view is faithful grayscale, but the figure is embedded beside a large right-hand control panel, shifting the at-a-glance composition away from the standalone centered tree of the source
evaluation.notes: The bottom-up merge lattice is structurally and numerically exact (5,2,4,7,1,3,2,6 -> [2,5][4,7][1,3][2,6] -> [2,4,5,7][1,2,3,6] -> 1,2,2,3,4,5,6,7) with correct upward arrowheads and 'merge' labels, and the added interactions (post-order merge-call highlighter, live merge-code editor with worker-based frame playback, and a stability trace distinguishing the two 2s) are deep, functional, and pedagogically on-point; the main weaknesses are the compressed tree proportions versus the source's wide layout and somewhat small merge labels.
action_items: Widen the lattice horizontally and reduce vertical row spacing (e.g. viewbox closer to 900x520 with rows at ~90px pitch) so the tree matches the source's wide landscape aspect ratio instead of a tall narrow one
Increase the 'merge' label font size (~16-18px) and nudge each label into the open gap between its two arrows to mirror the source's prominent centered placement
Consider giving the SVG container more horizontal share (or a wider min-width) so the tree is not squeezed into the left half beside the control panel at inline size

feedback.rationale: No failure modes, overall average of 4.4 with concept and interactivity at 5/5, and the remaining discrepancies are minor visual polish (aspect ratio and label sizing) that are unlikely to justify another iteration.
